en: Majjhima Nikāya 120,
Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta:
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the reappearance according to formations.”
“Listen to that and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Here, monks, a monk is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, endowed with generosity, and endowed with wisdom.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of wealthy kshatriyas!’”
Thus he fixes that mind, resolves upon that mind, and develops that mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and thus cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, he is endowed with virtue, he is endowed with learning, he is endowed with generosity, and he is endowed with wisdom.
It occurs to him:
“Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the wealthy brahmins... [and so on].
‘May I be reborn in the company of wealthy householders.
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon it, and develops that state of mind.
When those volitional formations and modes of abiding have been thus developed and cultivated, they lead to rebirth in that very state.
“Monks, this is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a monk is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, endowed with generosity, and endowed with wisdom.
He has heard this:”
‘The gods of the Four Great Kings are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings!’
Thus he fixes that mind, resolves upon that mind, and develops that mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, when thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth in that very place.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth in that very place.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, endowed with generosity, and endowed with wisdom.
He has heard:
"The Tāvatiṃsa devas... [and so on].
the Yāma devas … the Tusita devas … the Nimmānarati devas …
"The Paranimmitavasavatti devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the Paranimmitavasavatti devas!"
Thus he fixes that mind, resolves upon that mind, and develops that mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and thus cultivated, lead to rebirth in that very place.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth in that very place.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, endowed with generosity, and endowed with wisdom.
He has heard:
“The Brahmā Sahassa is long-lived, beautiful, and full of happiness.”
“Bhikkhus, the Brahmā Sahassa dwells pervading and resolving his mind upon a thousandfold world system.
He dwells pervading and resolving his mind upon whatever beings have been reborn there as well.
It is just as if, bhikkhus, a man with good eyesight were to take an apple in his hand and examine it.”
In the same way, monks, the Brahmā Sahassa dwells pervading and resolving his mind over a thousandfold world-system.
He dwells pervading and resolving his mind even over those beings who have been reborn there.
It occurs to him thus:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the thousandfold Brahmā!
He fixes his mind on this, resolves upon this, and develops this thought.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
"This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, ... endowed with generosity..."
He is endowed with wisdom.
He has heard:
"The Brahmā of Two Thousand... [and so on].
“A Brahmā of three thousand worlds...
a Brahmā of four thousand worlds...
a Brahmā of five thousand worlds is long-lived, beautiful, and possesses great happiness.”
“Bhikkhus, a Brahmā of five thousand abides pervading and resolving upon a world-system of five thousand worlds.
He abides pervading and resolving upon whatever beings have been reborn there as well.
Just as, bhikkhus, a man with good sight might take five myrobalan fruits in his hand and examine them;”
In the same way, monks, the Brahmā Pañcasahassa dwells having pervaded and resolved upon a five-thousandfold world system.
He dwells having pervaded and resolved upon whatever beings have been reborn there as well.
It occurs to him thus:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the five thousand Brahmās!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon it, and develops that state of mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, endowed with learning, [endowed with generosity]... [endowed with wisdom].
He is endowed with wisdom.
He has heard:
"The Brahmā of Ten Thousand is long-lived, beautiful, and abounding in happiness."
“Bhikkhus, the Brahmā of ten thousand worlds dwells pervading and resolving upon a ten-thousandfold world system.
He dwells pervading and resolving upon whatever beings have been reborn there.
Just as, bhikkhus, a beautiful beryl gem of pure birth, eight-faceted and well-cut, placed on a yellow cloth, gleams, glows, and radiates;”
In the same way, monks, the Brahmā of ten thousand abides pervading and resolving upon the ten-thousandfold world system;
he abides pervading and resolving upon whatever beings have been reborn there as well.
This thought occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the ten-thousandfold Brahmā!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that state of mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, ... with learning, ... [and so forth].
He is endowed with generosity … and wisdom.
He has heard:
‘The Brahmā of a hundred thousand is long-lived, beautiful, and full of happiness.
Monks, the Brahmā of a hundred thousand dwells pervading and resolving his mind over a world-system of a hundred thousand.
He dwells pervading and resolving his mind even over those beings who have been reborn there.
“Just as, monks, a nugget of gold from the Jambu River, well-refined by a skilled smith at the forge’s mouth and placed upon a pale cloth, shines, glows, and radiates;
even so, monks, the Brahmā of a hundred thousand abides pervading and resolving his mind over a world-system of a hundred thousand.
He abides pervading and resolving his mind over whatever beings have been reborn there as well.”
It occurs to him:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the Brahmā of a hundred thousandfold [world-system]!
He fixes his mind upon that, resolves his mind upon that, and develops that mind.
When those volitional formations and modes of abiding have been thus developed and cultivated by him, they lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a monk is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue...
He is endowed with learning, generosity, and wisdom.
He has heard:
"The Ābhā devas...
the Parittābhā devas..."
"The Appamāṇābha devas...
the Ābhassara devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him thus:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the Ābhassara devas!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that state of mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, [endowed with learning]... [endowed with generosity]... [endowed with wisdom].
He is endowed with generosity ... and wisdom.
He has heard this:
The Parittasubha devas...
the Appamāṇasubha devas...
and the Subhakiṇha devas have long life, are beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the Subhakiṇha devas!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that mind.
When those volitional formations and modes of abiding have been thus developed and cultivated by you, they lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a monk is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue...
He is endowed with learning, generosity, and wisdom.
He has heard:
"The Vehapphala devas...
the Aviha devas... [and so on].
the Atappa devas … the Sudassa devas … the Sudassi devas …
"The Akaniṭṭha devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
"Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the Akaniṭṭha devas!"
Thus he fixes that mind, resolves upon that mind, and develops that mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, when thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a monk is endowed with faith, with virtue,
with learning,
and with generosity.
He is endowed with wisdom.
He has heard:
"The gods who have reached the base of infinite space are long-lived, long-enduring, and abound in happiness."
It occurs to him:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the gods who have attained the base of infinite space!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that mind.
When those volitional formations and abidings of yours have been thus developed and cultivated, they lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue...
He is endowed with learning, generosity, and wisdom.
He has heard:
"The gods who have reached the base of infinite consciousness are long-lived, long-enduring, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the devas of the base of infinite consciousness!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that state of mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, [endowed with learning]… [endowed with generosity]… [endowed with wisdom].”
He is endowed with generosity … and wisdom.
He has heard this:
"The gods who have reached the sphere of nothingness...
the gods who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception are long-lived, long-enduring, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him thus:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the gods of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception!
He fixes his mind on that, resolves upon that, and develops that mind.
Those volitional formations and modes of abiding, thus developed and cultivated, lead to rebirth there.
This, monks, is the path, this is the way that leads to rebirth there.
Furthermore, monks, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, [endowed with learning]... [endowed with generosity]... [endowed with wisdom].
He is endowed with generosity … and wisdom.
It occurs to him thus:

‘Oh, that by the destruction of the taints, I might realize for myself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it, dwell therein.

He, by the destruction of the taints, realizes for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it, dwells therein.
This, monks, is the monk who is not reborn anywhere.”
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Saṅkhārupapatti Sutta, the tenth, is finished.
The second chapter, the Anupada-vagga, is finished.
Its summary verse is:
Anupada, Sodhana, and Porisadhamma.
The analysis of the many elements is to be cultivated;
the praise of the Buddha by name consists of forty [verses], as do the mindfulness of breathing,
the application of mindfulness to the body, and rebirth.
